rows: Start off by writing the term $c$ of the divisor on the left side. Here, $c = {\color{blue}{3}}.$ Then, write the coefficients of all terms of the dividend on the right side in descending order of their degree. Remember the sign! Also, if a term is missing, use $0$ as the coefficient.
Bring down the leading term of the dividend. Here, the leading term is ${\color{red}2}.$
Multiply the leading term $\color{red}2$ by ${\color{blue}3 }.$ This gives ${{\color{blue}{3}}\cdot \color{red}{2}} = {\color{green}6}.$ Place the result below the next term.

Add the last result ( $\color{green}{6}$ ) to the term located above ( $\color{magenta}{-5}$ ) and write their sum below the line. This gives ${\color{magenta}{-5}} + {\color{green}{6}}={\color{red}{1}}.$

We now repeat the process. Multiply the last result ( $\color{red}1$ here) by $\color{blue} 3$ and place the result below the next term. This gives ${\color{blue}{3}}\cdot {\color{red}{1}}= {\color{green}{3}}.$

Now add the last result ( $\color{green}{3}$ ) to the term located above ( $\color{magenta}{-7}$ ) and write their sum below the line. This gives ${\color{magenta}{-7}} + {\color{green}{3}}={\color{red}{-4}}.$

There is one last step. Again, multiply $\color{blue} 3$ by the last result $\color{red}-4$ and write it below the constant term. This gives ${\color{blue}{3}}\cdot{\color{red}{(-4)}}={\color{green}-12}.$ Finally, add $\color{green}-12$ to $\color{magenta}11$ to get ${\color{blue}{-1}},$ which is the remainder. The remainder $\color{blue}-1$ is important, so we put a box around it.
